concept.name: Dealer gamma
concept.definition: Dealer gamma is the net gamma position carried by options market makers as a consequence of filling customer order flow: when customers net-buy options, dealers end up short gamma and must hedge by trading with the market's direction; when customers net-sell, dealers are long gamma and hedge against the move. It describes positioning, not a tradable instrument.
concept.intuition: Dealers try to stay direction-neutral, so whatever convexity customers buy, dealers are short — and that forces them to buy high and sell low mechanically, which can amplify trends, or the reverse, which dampens them.
concept.mechanics: A dealer short a call is short delta and short gamma: as the underlying rises they must buy more of it to re-hedge, and as it falls they sell — same-direction flow. Aggregate dealer gamma therefore determines whether hedging stabilizes or destabilizes: Cboe's 0DTE analysis quantifies net market-maker gamma per strike and found it generally small because customer buy/sell flow is balanced.
concept.failure_modes: Dealer-gamma narratives are chronically over-extrapolated from unobservable positioning; even Cboe's transaction-level data show typical net exposures are a fraction of a percent of futures liquidity, so blaming dealer hedging for everyday moves usually misattributes cause. Positioning can also flip intraday as prices cross high-gamma strikes.
concept.misconceptions: Dealers do not hold views — they hold inventory to hedge, so 'dealers are short the market' confuses short gamma with directional shorting. Nor is dealer hedging automatically destabilizing: the sign of their net gamma, not its existence, determines the effect.
concept.example: Ahead of a large OPEX, if customers are net long SPX calls, dealers are short those calls and short gamma; a rally then forces them to buy futures into strength, mechanically adding to the move until positions roll off at expiration.

citations.source: Cboe — Volatility Insights: Evaluating the Market Impact of SPX 0DTE Options (Mandy Xu, 2023)
citations.section: What Is Gamma Hedging?; High Volume != High Risk
